brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
A family of hot teas drunk across the Arab world, usually strong and dark, often sweet, and commonly flavoured with spices or herbs such as cardamom, cinnamon, anise or spearmint.

This is a way of preparing tea more than a tea you buy under one name, so the recipe and the base tea change from one maker to the next.
history: It has been drunk for centuries and is tied to hospitality: it is served to guests and at business meetings, and turning down a cup can seem rude. One account credits Arab merchants on the Silk Road with bringing tea to the Middle East. Variants include cardamom, cinnamon and mint teas, the Bedouin tea made over an open fire, and herbal cups of sage, thyme or hibiscus.
processing: Made from a black base tea according to the recipe; the method varies.
harvest_season: Not tied to a harvest: it depends on the base tea.
appearance_dry: Usually dark twisted leaf, sometimes with golden tips.
taste_profile: Expect what black teas usually give: malty, sweet and brisk.
vintage_note: Not sold by vintage: it is made from whatever base tea the maker keeps, so freshness of the base matters more than the year.
